newsitem.title: UK: Rosneft sees no Transneft stake in CPC -- for now.
newsitem.headline: Rosneft sees no Transneft stake in CPC -- for now.

text.p: Russian oil company Rosneft on Thursday ruled out that pipeline operator Transneft will become a shareholder in the Caspian Pipeline Consortium (CPC), which is to build an oil pipeline from Kazakhstan to the Black Sea.
Transneft's position has been a controversial issue among CPC members, who last week signed a $2 billion deal to build the pipeline.

"Transneft is an operator of this project and Transneft is not and will not be a shareholder of this project," said Rosneft's president Alexander Putilov told journalists. But he added this principle was not "written in stone".

"What will happen in the future, only the future knows," Putilov told a news conference on the official signing of a venture agreement between Rosneft and Royal Dutch/Shell Group on jointly taking a 7.5 percent stake in CPC.
CPC counts a total of seven companies as its shareholders, while the Russian, Kazakh and Omani governments will hold respectively 24, 19 and seven percent.
Transneft told Reuters in Moscow on Friday that it wanted Russia's entire 24 percent stake.
Building of the pipeline is scheduled to begin by the end of September and planned to be completed in 1999.
